description: This case study from the Global Infrastructure Hub presents the Thames Tideway Tunnel, a 25 km tunnel beneath the River Thames in central London, as a showcase infrastructure project. The page states a cost of 4.2 billion pounds at the time and describes it as the largest sewer improvement project in the UK for over a century, connecting to 34 existing combined sewer overflows owned by Thames Water. Because of the scale, complexity and the utility's own capital programme, the tunnel was procured through a separate provider that would become a new Ofwat-regulated utility, selected competitively on the lowest bid weighted average cost of capital and deliverability. Bazalgette Tunnel Limited, later known as Tideway, won and was licensed by Ofwat; Thames Water will operate the tunnel as part of the London network while Tideway maintains it, and customers pay through their bills. The Global Infrastructure Hub is a G20 initiative that documents good practice. Coverage: one project in London, with the situation as of April 2017. Access: free web page; licence not stated. Caveats: the cost and status are those of 2017 and later figures differ; the page is a summary, not a data source. It supports investment appraisal and combined sewer overflow control planning, and relates to the Environment Agency storm overflow returns in the catalogue.
